gap: Acceptance check for A: at about 2 m, waist-up, the character must pass as a real person. The skin must show specular breakup and subsurface warmth instead of uniform plastic albedo, and the hair must have a strand or clump silhouette with no solid shell edge. The arms must be anatomically proportioned, with the elbow near waist height. The fingers must fully wrap the held object, with a visible contact shadow where the hand meets it.

Judge: Image B is clearly better in all four pairs, and none of the calls was close. The four A frames look like they come from the same build. Pairs 1 and 4 share the same colonnade-and-tile set, and all four share the same character look. They have some real strengths: warm practical bloom, a pleasant golden-hour haze with sun flare in pair 2, and reasonable crowd counts in pairs 2-4. Character fidelity is the main thing holding them back, and it is the main subject of this set. The A characters have mannequin skin with uniform albedo and no specular breakup or subsurface warmth. Their faces are smeared or flat with no self-shadowing, and their hair is a helmet-like shell. Their idle poses are stiff, with odd arm proportions and limp grips that do not wrap the held object. Props are faceted or untextured (umbrellas, bags, white cards), and pair 3 shows ghosting and contorted poses. NPCs walk in single-file lines and have no individual behaviors or narrative. Each A frame also has placeholder surfaces that break immersion: black void doorways, blank white panels, pastel color-block storefronts, untextured slabs and primitive shelters. The practical lights also fail to light the characters. The B frames win on hero-character detail, purposeful hand-to-prop interaction, distinct per-pedestrian activity, storytelling set dressing and deliberate cinematic composition. Only the B frames in pairs 2 and 3 truly wowed. For the in-development build, the priorities in order are: (1) character skin and hair shading, plus correct lighting response to the scene's practicals; (2) hand-to-prop grip IK and anatomically correct poses; (3) varied ambient behaviors, with gaze directed away from the camera; (4) removing placeholder geometry and adding dressed storefronts and interiors.
